```{r}
df <- read_csv("C:/Users/apmc/OneDrive - Norwegian University of Life Sciences/BatLab Norway/Projects/CoastalMonitoring/Analyses/Outputs/Reed/CombineCSVs_Report2026_2026-11-11/CM_manualIDs_allavailable_subsets.csv")

dim(df)
# 89556    14
names(df)
str(df)

DF <- df |> 
  dplyr::select(-1) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    autoid = factor(autoid),
    manualid = factor(manualid), 
    analyst = factor(analyst), 
    site = factor(site),
    newauto = factor(newauto),
    DATE = as.Date(DATE), 
    DATE.12 = as.Date(DATE.12), 
    TIME = as.character(TIME), 
    TIME.12 = as.character(TIME.12))  

summary(DF)
names(DF)
# Looking good! 

```

```{r}
## Overview of which sites have been validated when 
ggplot(DF) + 
  geom_point(aes(x= DATE, y = site, color = analyst), 
             size = 3, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() + xlab("")  + ylab("")

ggplot(DF |> filter(analyst != "Reed April McKay") |> droplevels()) + 
  geom_point(aes(x= DATE, y = site, color = analyst), 
             size = 3, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() + xlab("")  + ylab("") + 
  ggtitle ("Overview of manually verified data - 2024 only")

summary(DF)
summary(DF$newauto)
summary(DF$manualid)
summary(DF$site)

```


## Check agreement manual vs autoid - Myotis 
```{r}
## Check agreement manual vs autoid - Myotis 
summary(DF$newauto)
summary(DF$manualid)
summary(DF$site)

mysp <- DF |> 
  dplyr::filter(manualid %in% c("MYSP", "MDAU") | newauto == "MYSP") |> 
           droplevels() 

summary(mysp)
## Matches what we expect from the df1
dim(mysp)
# 9253   13

## Check the amount of agreement between autoid and manual id 

#Logistic regression to determine cut-off
mysp_data <- DF %>%
  dplyr::filter(newauto == "MYSP") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    mratio = as.numeric(MATCH.RATIO),
    correct = ifelse(manualid%in% c("MYSP", "MDAU"), 1, 0)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(MATCH.RATIO))

dim(mysp_data)
# 4576   15

ggplot2::ggplot(mysp_data) + 
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = MATCH.RATIO, y = correct))

mysp_glm <- glm(
  correct ~ MATCH.RATIO,
  family = binomial,
  data = mysp_data)

summary(mysp_glm)
# Coefficients:
#             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
# (Intercept)   0.4140     0.1998   2.072   0.0382 *  
# MATCH.RATIO   4.3016     0.3531  12.184   <2e-16 ***
# ---
# Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
# 
# (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
# 
#     Null deviance: 1680.1  on 4575  degrees of freedom
# Residual deviance: 1513.3  on 4574  degrees of freedom
# AIC: 1517.3
# 
# Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 6

### Now visualize the level of agreement between KPRO and Frode based on this model 
# Lagny data for kurven
newdata <- data.frame(MATCH.RATIO = seq(min(mysp_data$MATCH.RATIO),
                                   max(mysp_data$MATCH.RATIO),
                                   length.out = 200))
newdata$pred <- predict(mysp_glm, newdata, type = "response")

# Show the level of agreement between manual id and autoid
ggplot2::ggplot(mysp_data, ggplot2::aes(x = MATCH.RATIO, y = correct)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = newdata, ggplot2::aes(x = MATCH.RATIO, y = pred),
            color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "KPRO match ratio", y = "Predicted probability of correct") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Comparing KPRO vs Manual ID for Myotis species")

# calculates the match ratio cut-off by inverting the logistic regression
get_cutoff <- function(p, model) {
  beta0 <- coef(model)[1]
  beta1 <- coef(model)[2]
  (log(p / (1 - p)) - beta0) / beta1
}


# target probabilities for which we want to know the match ratio
target_probs <- c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9)

#library(clustur)
# create table with probability column and fill with values from get-cutoff + lost and retained calls + percentage
loss_table <- data.frame(Probability = target_probs) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Cutoff_Ratio = pmin(
      sapply(Probability, get_cutoff, model = mysp_glm),
      1),
    Calls_retained = sapply(Cutoff_Ratio, function(c) 
      sum(mysp_data$mratio >= c)),
    Calls_lost = sapply(Cutoff_Ratio, function(c) 
      sum(mysp_data$mratio < c)),
    Percent_loss = round(
      (Calls_lost / nrow(mysp_data)) * 100, 2 ) )

#   Probability Cutoff_Ratio Calls_retained Calls_lost Percent_loss
# 1        0.50  -0.79763941           5995          0         0.00
# 2        0.60  -0.58093577           5995          0         0.00
# 3        0.70  -0.34479520           5995          0         0.00
# 4        0.80  -0.05672478           5995          0         0.00
# 5        0.85   0.12943015           5989          6         0.10
# 6        0.90   0.37668250           5417        578         9.64

## Looks like a .37 Match Ratio is a good estimate 

```

  dplyr::mutate(
    mratio = as.numeric(MATCH.RATIO),

NYCT_glm <- glm(

summary(NYCT_glm)

# Lagny data for kurven
newdata <- data.frame(MATCH.RATIO = seq(min(NYCT_data$MATCH.RATIO),
                                   max(NYCT_data$MATCH.RATIO),
                                   length.out = 200))

# Show the level of agreement between manual id and autoid
ggplot2::ggplot(NYCT_data, ggplot2::aes(x = MATCH.RATIO, y = correct)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = newdata, ggplot2::aes(x = MATCH.RATIO, y = pred),
            color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "KPRO match ratio", y = "Predicted probability of correct") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Comparing KPRO vs Manual ID for Nyctaloids - with auto Noctules")

# calculates the match ratio cut-off by inverting the logistic regression
get_cutoff <- function(p, model) {
  beta0 <- coef(model)[1]
  beta1 <- coef(model)[2]
  (log(p / (1 - p)) - beta0) / beta1
}


# target probabilities for which we want to know the match ratio
target_probs <- c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9)

#library(clustur)
# create table with probability column and fill with values from get-cutoff + lost and retained calls + percentage
loss_table <- data.frame(Probability = target_probs) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Cutoff_Ratio = pmin(
      sapply(Probability, get_cutoff, model = NYCT_glm),
      1),
    Calls_retained = sapply(Cutoff_Ratio, function(c) 
      sum(NYCT_data$mratio >= c)),
    Calls_lost = sapply(Cutoff_Ratio, function(c) 
      sum(NYCT_data$mratio < c)),
    Percent_loss = round(
      (Calls_lost / nrow(NYCT_data)) * 100, 2 ) )

print(loss_table)
#   Probability Cutoff_Ratio Calls_retained Calls_lost Percent_loss

# 2        0.60            1           1329       3027        69.49

# 4        0.80            1           1329       3027        69.49
# 5        0.85            1           1329       3027        69.49
# 6        0.90            1           1329       3027        69.49
